arxiv-2012-11335.title: Spontaneous imbibition dynamics in interacting multi-capillary systems: A generalized model
arxiv-2012-11335.creator: Shabina Ashraf, Yves Méheust, Jyoti Phirani
arxiv-2012-11335.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Shabina Ashraf, Yves Méheust, Jyoti Phirani. Bundle-of-tubes model was previously used to understand the flow behaviour in a porous medium. The interacting nature of the pores within a porous medium can be well depicted by an interacting capillary model. However, the arrangement of pores is crucial in understanding the flow behaviour in an interacting capillary system, which also leads to different governing equations of spontaneous imbibition.

arxiv-2110-06817.title: Optical Character Recognition of 19 th Century Classical Commentaries: the Current State of Affairs Thanks: This version of the article corresponds to the accepted manuscript. For the final published version see https://doi.org/10.1145/3476887.3476911 .
arxiv-2110-06817.creator: Matteo Romanello, Sven Najem-Meyer, Bruce Robertson
arxiv-2110-06817.description: Abstract Together with critical editions and translations, commentaries are one of the main genres of publication in literary and textual scholarship, and have a century-long tradition. Yet, the exploitation of thousands of digitized historical commentaries was hitherto hindered by the poor quality of Optical Character Recognition (OCR), especially on commentaries to Greek texts.

arxiv-2403-14891.title: Creep-enhanced vortex pinning revealed through nonmonotonic relaxation of the Campbell length
arxiv-2403-14891.creator: Sunil Ghimire, Filippo Gaggioli, Kamal R. Joshi, Marcin Kończykowski, Romain Grasset, Elizabeth H. Krenkel, Amlan Datta, Makariy A. Tanatar, Shuzhang Chen, Cedomir Petrovic, Vadim B. Geshkenbein, Ruslan Prozorov
arxiv-2403-14891.description: Abstract We study the effects of flux creep on the linear AC response of the vortex lattice in single crystals Ca 3 Ir 4 Sn 13 by measuring the Campbell penetration depth, λ C ​ ( T , H , t ) \lambda_{\rm\scriptscriptstyle C}(T,H,t) .

arxiv-2404-16083.title: Constant-depth preparation of matrix product states with adaptive quantum circuits
arxiv-2404-16083.creator: Kevin C. Smith, Abid Khan, Bryan K. Clark, S.M. Girvin, Tzu-Chieh Wei
arxiv-2404-16083.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Kevin C. Smith, Abid Khan, Bryan K. Clark, S.M. Girvin, Tzu-Chieh Wei. Adaptive quantum circuits, which combine local unitary gates, midcircuit measurements, and feedforward operations, have recently emerged as a promising avenue for efficient state preparation, particularly on near-term quantum devices limited to shallow-depth circuits. Matrix product states (MPS) comprise a significant class of many-body entangled states, efficiently describing the ground states of one-dimensional gapped local Hamiltonians and finding applications in a number of recent quantum algorithms.

arxiv-2409-16503.title: GOALS-JWST: Constraining the Emergence Timescale for Massive Star Clusters in NGC 3256
arxiv-2409-16503.creator: Sean T. Linden, Thomas Lai, Aaron S. Evans, Lee Armus, Kirsten L. Larson, Jeffrey A. Rich, Vivian U, George C. Privon, Hanae Inami, Yiqing Song, Marina Bianchin, Thomas Bohn, Victorine A. Buiten, Maria Sanchez-García, Justin Kader, Laura Lenkić, Anne M. Medling, Torsten Böker, Tanio Díaz-Santos, Vas
arxiv-2409-16503.description: Abstract We present the results of a James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) NIRCam and NIRSpec investigation into the young massive star cluster (YMC) population of NGC 3256, the most cluster-rich luminous infrared galaxy (LIRG) in the Great Observatories All Sky LIRG Survey.

arxiv-2505-08303.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Black-Box Prompt Optimization as the Scale of LLMs Continues to Grow
arxiv-2505-08303.creator: Ziyu Zhou, Yihang Wu, Jingyuan Yang, Zhan Xiao, Rongjun Li
arxiv-2505-08303.description: Abstract Black-Box prompt optimization methods have emerged as a promising strategy for refining input prompts to better align large language models (LLMs), thereby enhancing their task performance. Although these methods have demonstrated encouraging results, most studies and experiments have primarily focused on smaller-scale models (e.g., 7B, 14B) or earlier versions (e.g., GPT-3.5) of LLMs.

arxiv-2505-15428.title: Likelihood Variance as Text Importance for Resampling Texts to Map Language Models
arxiv-2505-15428.creator: Momose Oyama, Ryo Kishino, Hiroaki Yamagiwa, Hidetoshi Shimodaira
arxiv-2505-15428.description: Abstract We address the computational cost of constructing a model map, which embeds diverse language models into a common space for comparison via KL divergence. The map relies on log-likelihoods over a large text set, making the cost proportional to the number of texts.

arxiv-2510-21887.title: Generative AI in Depth: A Survey of Recent Advances, Model Variants, and Real-World Applications
arxiv-2510-21887.creator: Shamim Yazdani 1 , Akansha Singh 2 , Nripsuta Saxena 3 , Zichong Wang 1 , Avash Palikhe 1 , Deng Pan 1 , Umapada Pal 4 , Jie Yang 5, Wenbin Zhang
arxiv-2510-21887.description: Abstract In recent years, deep learning based generative models, particularly Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), and Diffusion Models (DMs), have been instrumental in in generating diverse, high-quality content across various domains, such as image and video synthesis. This capability has led to widespread adoption of these models and has captured strong public interest.

pmc-10738091.title: CO-DESIGNING A STAGE 1B FEASIBILITY STUDY OF INPATIENT PALLIATIVE COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKER SUPPORT
pmc-10738091.creator: Jung Kwak, Elizabeth Kvale, Sarah Mills, Snehal Patel
pmc-10738091.description: Persons living with dementia (PLWD) are 2-3 times more likely than their non-dementia peers to be hospitalized annually and experience burdensome care transitions and treatments at the late stage of dementia. Minoritized PLWDs are significantly more likely to be hospitalized and experience frequent transitions between care settings, and also less likely to access palliative care.

pmc-12430188.title: The Influence of Selected Properties of Sintered Iron Doped with Lubricants on Its Tribological Properties
pmc-12430188.creator: Wiesław Urbaniak, Tomasz Majewski, Grzegorz Śmigielski, Anna Trynda, Aneta D Petelska, Alexander Yu Churyumov, Ruitao Qu
pmc-12430188.description: This study investigated materials intended for use in porous bearings, incorporating selected layered materials. Previous research has demonstrated that layered compounds, such as molybdenum disulfide (MoS2), tungsten disulfide (WS2), and hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN), can significantly enhance tribological performance. However, these improvements in tribological properties may be accompanied by undesirable characteristics that could limit the practical application of such materials.

pmc-12561570.title: Genome-Wide Analysis of the Thiamine Biosynthesis Gene Families in Common Bean Reveals Their Crucial Roles Conferring Resistance to Fusarium Wilt
pmc-12561570.creator: Ming Feng, Yu Liu, Yang Zhao, Tao Li, Jian Chen, Yuning Huang, Weide Ge, Chao Zhong, Renfeng Xue, Feng Zhang
pmc-12561570.description: Simple SummaryFusarium wilt is a devastating soil-borne disease that can reduce common bean yields by up to 50% in severely affected regions worldwide. In this study, five key thiamine biosynthetic genes were identified in common bean, all showing evolutionary conservation across plant species. These genes exhibited distinct activity in different plant organs.

pmc-12578697.title: Association of anterior communicating artery location with rupture in small intracranial aneurysms less than 5 mm: a retrospective analysis
pmc-12578697.creator: Shin Heon Lee, Kyoung Min Jang, Taek Kyun Nam, Hyun Ho Choi
pmc-12578697.description: Despite intracranial aneurysms smaller than 5 mm are generally considered to have a low risk of rupture, management of those located at the anterior communicating artery (ACoA) remains a significant clinical challenge. This study examined the association between ACoA location and rupture tendency in aneurysms smaller than 5 mm.

pmc-12696696.title: NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation Modulates Neutrophil Extracellular Trap Formation and Aggravates Airway Inflammation in Bronchiectasis
pmc-12696696.creator: Zhao-ming Chen, Jia-hui He, Rui-di Tang, Jun-qing Yue, Xiao-xian Zhang, Zhen-feng He, Shao-qiang Li, Hui-min Li, Xiao-fen Zhang, Lai-jian Cen, Cui-xia Pan, Ming-xin Shi, Sheng-zhu Lin, Shu-jun Guo, Wei-jie Guan
pmc-12696696.description: Neutrophilic inflammation and Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection have been implicated in the pathogenesis and progression of bronchiectasis. However, the mechanisms underlying the inflammasome activation and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) formation, which are triggered by lipopolysaccharide (LPS), thereby fostering relentless neutrophilic inflammation and airway destruction, remain poorly understood.

pmc-12981653.title: Interpretable machine learning for identifying ICU readmission risk in subgroups with probabilistic rules
pmc-12981653.creator: Lincen Yang, Siri L van der Meijden, Sesmu M Arbous, Matthijs van Leeuwen
pmc-12981653.description: ObjectiveEstimating readmission risk for intensive care unit (ICU) patients is critical for clinicians to optimize resource allocation and prevent premature discharges. Machine learning models currently applied to this task either lack interpretability or cannot identify patient subgroups with distinctive readmission risks and characteristics.

pmc-13458271.title: Effectiveness of different non-surgical scar reduction methods in post-operative scars: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13458271.creator: Genevieve Chin Xuen Heng, Zhao Qi Charles Wang, Rachel Xue Ning Lee, Clement Luck Khng Chia
pmc-13458271.description: BackgroundEffective scar management is crucial in improving cosmetic outcomes, restoring physiological function, and supporting psychological well-being in surgical patients. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to evaluate the effectiveness of post-operative scar reduction techniques in optimising wound healing and minimising scar formation.

uslaw-usc-t22-s4102.title: 22 U.S.C. § 4102 — Definitions
uslaw-usc-t22-s4102.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t22-s4102.description: United States Code, Title 22 (Foreign Relations And Intercourse); Chapter 52 (Foreign Service); Subchapter X (Labor-Management Relations). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. As used in this subchapter, the term— (1) “Authority” means the Federal Labor Relations Authority, described in section 7104(a) of title 5; (2) “Board” means the Foreign Service Labor Relations Board, established by section 4106(a) of this title; (3) “collective.
